name: AZ-09
label: Likely R

key_factors: Deep Republican lean of the district (R+15) with incumbent Paul Gosar seeking another term
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at only about 3 percent
Dani Sterbinsky reports just $26,000 cash on hand versus Gosar's $303,000 after spending down her primary fundraising
No public polls or expert ratings of the race, leaving fundamentals to carry the forecast
model.rationale: The seat's strong Republican lean plus Gosar's incumbency would require a large unanticipated shift for a Democrat to win, and Sterbinsky's thin general-election war chest gives her little means to force one. Markets pricing the race near 3 percent Democratic and the absence of any polling suggesting competitiveness point to keeping expectations close to the district's underlying margin.
model.watch: Heavy late outside spending against Gosar or a major scandal could tighten the race, but nothing of the kind appears in the current record.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's ninth district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, and Paul Gosar has held it comfortably through multiple cycles. He returns as the incumbent with a renomination in hand and about $303,000 in cash on hand. Democrat Dani Sterbinsky raised roughly $354,000 for the race, but reports only about $26,000 available heading into the general election, leaving her little financial cushion in a district that leans heavily against her party.

No public polls of the race are available, and major race raters have not scored it, so expectations rest on the district's fundamentals. Prediction markets give Gosar roughly a 94 percent chance of winning. Absent an outside shock, such as a scandal or a surge of late outside spending, the seat appears very likely to remain in Republican hands.
